evals.prompt: I bumped longhorn_version from 1.11.1 to 1.12.1 and ran terraform apply on all three clusters last week. Everything is green, but server1 shows 85% CPU requested while it barely does anything. Is the upgrade done?
evals.expected_output: Runs the instance-manager detection on every cluster, identifies any v1.11.1 IM still hosting engines as stale and as the reservation, explains that a pod restart will not move the engines, and lays out the cordon → delete pods → wait for detached → uncordon procedure with the dump, operator confirmation, OpenBao unseal and miot-bridge checks — then re-runs detection until only 1.12.1 IMs remain.
expectations: Queries instancemanagers.longhorn.io on server1, server2 and server3, not only server1
Treats an IM whose image is not v1.12.1 and still lists engines as stale
States that rollout restart / deleting a pod alone does not detach the volume on a single-node cluster
Maps the stale IM to its volumes and the pods mounting them before deleting anything
Asks the operator before the detach and takes a dump-all.sh dump first
Uses cordon, not drain, and uncordons only after every volume reads detached
Stops and waits for the operator to unseal OpenBao when server3 is involved, then force-syncs an ExternalSecret and checks refreshTime moves
Checks miot-bridge subscriptions after EMQX restarts on server1
Re-runs detection until one NEW-image IM per node remains and volumes are attached and healthy

evals.prompt: I changed only gitops/helm-values/server3/loki.yaml to raise retention and pushed it 20 minutes ago. ArgoCD says loki is Synced and Healthy. Is the new retention live?
evals.expected_output: Does not trust Synced: compares the app's status.sync.revisions with git rev-parse origin/main, recognises the stale multi-source values cache, checks git log for other unsynced commits before a hard refresh, hard-refreshes and syncs once, then verifies the running config rather than the pin.
expectations: Compares status.sync.revision(s) with git rev-parse origin/main
Names the values-only stale multi-source cache as the reason Synced can be wrong
Warns that a hard refresh reconciles every app with unsynced commits and checks git log first
Triggers exactly one sync and does not loop syncs
Verifies on the cluster (rendered config or running pod), not by the Synced badge

evals.prompt: Renovate wants to bump the mongodb chart. I also plan a Talos upgrade on server1 next week. Anything to watch for?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the mongodb chart does not pin the binary (bitnami/mongodb:latest), that a digest pin is deliberately not used and should not be proposed, that the Talos upgrade's fresh pull can move mongod irreversibly, and asks for a dump plus a comparison of mongod --version with what latest resolves to before the node work.
expectations: States the chart targetRevision does not decide the mongod version
Does not propose pinning the MongoDB image by digest
Links the Talos upgrade (fresh pull) to an irreversible MongoDB data-file upgrade
Requires a dump before the Talos upgrade
Renders OLD and NEW chart with this repo's values and diffs them before merging the bump
